call_vintage: as of Tue Nov 24, 07:00 GMT tape

changes.balance: The break was priced on flows and balances that can be checked this week, and the Canadian front tightened into it, which says the selling was global flat price rather than basin barrels; a thin week and a short book already at the largest of the year cut both ways from here.
changes.body: WTI Jan27 settled $80.17, down $3.24 or 3.88 percent, its lowest close since August 10, and Brent Jan27 settled $89.37, down $3.20 or 3.46 percent, its lowest close since August 31 (Reuters, Nov 23). Tuesday in Asia drifted near those lows, with Brent at $89.10 and WTI at $79.97 at 0700 GMT (Reuters, Nov 24). The board behind the break includes Libya's Sharara pipeline reopening, a Deutsche Bank estimate of a 52 million barrel global observed inventory build in October, an IEA October supply print of 105.4 million barrels a day, and a preliminary Reuters poll pointing to United States stock builds for the week ending Nov 20.
changes.conditional: A Wednesday EIA print that confirms the builds extends the surplus pricing; a draw against the poll, in a thin week with length already cut to the lowest of the year, is the squeeze setup.
changes.delta: Monday settles: WTI Jan27 $80.17 (-$3.24), Brent Jan27 $89.37 (-$3.20), lowest closes since August; Tuesday 0700 GMT Brent $89.10, WTI $79.97
changes.title: Monday settled three dollars lower on both benchmarks, at the lowest closes since August
changes.vintage: Monday settlements and Tuesday 0700 GMT tape, Nov 23-24, 2026

changes.balance: A mine claim that grows in number without gaining a named vessel is a narrative instrument until a second source confirms a hull; the market has stopped paying for this class of headline, and the one hard traffic number, four crossings with two tankers on Monday, cuts against the recovery framing rather than for either claim.
changes.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said on Monday that three tankers described as violating the strait rules caught fire after hitting naval mines, with the added claim that it happened despite a United States escort (Press TV and IRNA via Reuters, Nov 24). This follows Sunday's claim of two supertankers north of Ghanam Island. No vessel has been named in either version, the two counts may overlap, and no CENTCOM comment on the Monday claim was located. Sunday's separate Chabahar incident also remains without a named vessel, owner or damage through Nov 24. AIS-visible crossings counted 4 commercial ships on Nov 23, two of them tankers, with a seven-day average of 7.1 a day against a pre-crisis 84.8 a day (hormuz.now, Nov 24).
changes.conditional: A named vessel, an owner statement or a satellite confirmation converts this into a priced event; continued silence by Wednesday leaves it in the same class as the prior weekend's unverified mine claim.
changes.delta: Iranian claim enlarged from two tankers (Nov 22) to three (Nov 23), still unnamed and unverified; AIS-visible crossings on Nov 23 were 4 ships, 2 tankers
changes.source: Press TV and IRNA via Reuters, Nov 24, 2026; hormuz.now, updated Nov 24, 2026
changes.title: Iran enlarged its mine claim to three tankers, with no vessel named and no verification
changes.vintage: Iranian statements, Nov 22-23, 2026; crossing count to Nov 24, 08:01 UTC

changes.balance: The front tightening on a near four percent flat price break, with the location spread orderly, is the destination discount pattern rather than a trapped basin: the pressure is arriving through flat price and destination markets, not through egress at home.
changes.body: January WCS paper settled -$21.00 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 23), tightening $0.65 on 200 lots, with February at -$20.95 and March at -$20.15. January Houston WCS paper settled -$13.50 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 23), which puts the January ARV to TMW spread at +$7.50, orderly. January SYN settled +$5.90 (ICE TMS settle, Nov 23), which puts SYN to WCS at $26.90 on January, and January C5 settled +$7.00 (ICE TMF settle, Nov 23). The validated diesel crack is $72.94 and the 3-2-1 crack is $38.02 on the latest print dated Nov 24.
changes.conditional: A blowing out location spread or a storage bid would flip the read to egress binding at home; neither signature is present in the Nov 23 settlements.
changes.delta: January TMW paper -$21.00 (+$0.65) on Nov 23 settlements; January ARV to TMW spread +$7.50; diesel crack $72.94 validated Nov 24
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 23, 2026; validated crack history, refreshed Nov 24, 2026
changes.title: The Canadian front tightened into the flat price break, with the location spread orderly

flags.body: Sunday's confirmed incident near Chabahar and Iran's mine claims, enlarged on Monday from two tankers to three, all lack a named vessel, and the last measured strait clearance is 8.5 million barrels a day through Nov 16, about 50 percent of pre-war, while AIS-visible crossings were 4 ships on Nov 23 with two tankers. Wire lines that Hormuz shipments have returned to pre-war levels are not confirmed by these gauges for the strait itself.
flags.title: Chabahar incident and enlarged mine claim unverified, and the strait gauges stay near half of pre-war
flags.trigger: A named vessel or owner statement on either item, a fresh measured clearance print, or a confirmed cargo loss or closure

flags.body: The North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption has curtailed the system since Nov 14 with no restart timeline published, entering its eleventh day on Tuesday. Producers were trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access delivery points with tanks filling, and force majeure declarations stand at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX. The refinery receipt suspensions reported are of Bakken crude; no WCS buyer outage has been reported.
flags.title: North Dakota Pipeline disruption, day eleven
flags.trigger: An Enbridge restart notice or a published restart timeline for the North Dakota Pipeline

flags.body: The Houthi military spokesperson warned shipping companies to remove vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports, naming Jeddah, Yanbu, Jazan and King Fahd Industrial Port as potential targets (DeepDraft, Nov 22), and a Nov 22 claim of a hit on the Petro Rabigh refinery has no damage indication and no Saudi confirmation. Yanbu is the Red Sea outlet of the East-West pipeline and the Gulf system's second-largest loading terminal. Nothing has been confirmed hit, nothing has closed and no evacuation order has been issued.
flags.title: Yanbu on a named threat list
flags.trigger: Any strike on a Saudi Red Sea port, a port closure notice, or a mandatory evacuation order from Saudi port authorities
